sections.markdown:
## Signals, pedestrian beacons, markings and roundabouts

FACT_ID: sec10-R01 | anchor: A01
Pavement markings warn, direct and regulate traffic, as signs do. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=37]

FACT_ID: sec10-R02 | anchor: A01
A transverse white stop line marks the stopping position for a traffic control. Stop at that line rather than beside the sign or signal; the handbook describes an urban placement about 4 feet before the crosswalk. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=37]

FACT_ID: sec10-R03 | anchor: A01
White crosswalk markings may span all or part of the pavement or use a ladder pattern. Pedestrians in the crosswalk have priority over motor traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=37]

FACT_ID: sec10-R04 | anchor: A01
A marked crosswalk can occur midblock as well as at an intersection, sometimes with a pedestrian signal at the crossing. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=37]

FACT_ID: sec10-R05 | anchor: A01
A railroad approach may carry a large pavement X with the letters R on either side. A yellow centerline-side marking prevents passing, and active train warnings require a stop. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=37]

FACT_ID: sec10-R06 | anchor: A01
A centerline separates opposing traffic. On a two-lane road, a broken yellow centerline permits passing in either direction only when safe. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=37]

FACT_ID: sec10-R07 | anchor: A01
A solid yellow line on your side of a two-lane centerline prohibits passing there. If both centerlines are solid, neither direction may pass. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=37]

FACT_ID: sec10-R08 | anchor: A01
Dashed double white lane markings permit crossing into the neighboring lane; solid double white markings prohibit changing lanes across them. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=37]

FACT_ID: sec10-R09 | anchor: A01
Solid white edge lines show the side of the pavement, especially helpful after dark. A yellow left edge line can warn of a raised or narrow median. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=37]

FACT_ID: sec10-R10 | anchor: A01
Broken white lane lines divide lanes carrying traffic in the same direction. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=37]

FACT_ID: sec10-R11 | anchor: A01
On a road with at least 4 lanes and opposing flows, double solid yellow lines separate directions. The handbook permits crossing them only for a left turn into or from a street, driveway, private road or alley. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=37]

FACT_ID: sec10-R12 | anchor: A01
On a multilane road, stay right except when passing traffic moving in the same direction. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=37]

FACT_ID: sec10-R13 | anchor: A01
Diagonal yellow striping identifies a narrowing or obstruction area; keep to the right of that marked area. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=37]

FACT_ID: sec10-R14 | anchor: A02
A shared center turn lane is reserved for left turns, not general travel. Enter it no earlier than 300 feet before the intended left turn. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=38]

FACT_ID: sec10-R15 | anchor: A02
Before entering a two-direction center turn lane, check carefully for an opposing driver entering it to turn left. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=38]

FACT_ID: sec10-R16 | anchor: A02
A bicycle lane is usually separated by a solid white line near the right road edge; where a right-turn-only lane exists, the bicycle lane lies to its left to accommodate through cyclists. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=38]

FACT_ID: sec10-R17 | anchor: A02
Do not drive or park in a bicycle lane except when crossing it for a turn, and yield to bicyclists before that crossing. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=38]

FACT_ID: sec10-R18 | anchor: A02
Enter a roundabout toward the right and circulate counterclockwise, yielding to traffic already circulating. Exit by turning toward the right. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=38]

FACT_ID: sec10-R19 | anchor: A02
At a single-lane roundabout, slow to the advisory speed, stop for pedestrians at the approach crosswalk and wait for an opening in circulating traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=38]

FACT_ID: sec10-R20 | anchor: A02
Before the roundabout exit, signal the intended departure and stop for pedestrians in the exit crosswalk. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=38]

FACT_ID: sec10-R21 | anchor: A02
For a multilane roundabout, choose the correct lane before entering by following the lane signs and pavement arrows. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=38]

FACT_ID: sec10-R22 | anchor: A02
Entering a multilane roundabout requires yielding to circulating vehicles in both lanes. Keep the chosen lane while entering and circulating; do not change lanes within the roundabout. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=38]

FACT_ID: sec10-R23 | anchor: A02
A pedestrian should use the roundabout's crossing and refuge, checking that vehicles stop before each crossing stage, and must not walk to the center island. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=38]

FACT_ID: sec10-R24 | anchor: A02
An experienced cyclist may ride through a roundabout with traffic, using the center of the lane and stopping for crosswalk pedestrians. Children or riders uncomfortable in traffic should walk their bicycles and follow pedestrian rules. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=38]

FACT_ID: sec10-R25 | anchor: A02
The handbook's roundabout drawings are examples and do not represent every roundabout design. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ga-c:georgia-department-of-driver-services:handbook#pdf_page=38]

Misconceptions: A normally dark pedestrian hybrid beacon and a failed ordinary traffic signal have different meanings; a flashing red indication still requires a complete stop.
Mnemonic: Identify the device, read its phase, yield, then move.
Glossary: A hybrid beacon is a pedestrian-activated control; a center turn lane serves left turns from either direction; a refuge divides a pedestrian crossing into stages.
Dynamic-fact isolation: Graphic interpretation, current marking standards and visual asset rights remain separately reviewed; artwork is not reconstructed from garbled extraction.
